category.intro: Chanrai Nigeria supplies BYD battery-electric forklifts and warehouse equipment, from compact pallet trucks to 8-tonne counterbalance trucks and heavy tow tractors. Every truck runs on lithium iron phosphate batteries that charge during breaks, with no fumes and no battery watering. Our technicians maintain and repair them at your warehouse or factory, so your equipment stays on site.
category.salesBlurb: We help you choose the right BYD electric trucks for your loads, racking, aisles, shifts and power supply, and plan chargers and site layout with you.
category.serviceBlurb: Our technicians come to your site for repairs, planned maintenance, battery and charger checks, and operator training, so your trucks stay where they work.

brand.name: BYD
brand.about: BYD began in 1995 as a rechargeable-battery manufacturer and now builds electric vehicles, batteries and material handling equipment. Its forklift division makes battery-electric counterbalance forklifts, pallet trucks, stackers, reach trucks, tow tractors and logistics robots. BYD develops the trucks, the lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery cells and the chargers in-house and designs them to work together. Its electric counterbalance range spans roughly 1.6 to 8 tonnes.

Battery tested for low-temperature operation at -40 °C

families.name: EL-PRO Series Counterbalance Forklifts
families.summary: BYD's EL-PRO series of 2.0–3.8 t electric counterbalance forklifts for warehouses, docks and yards.
families.howItWorks:
An **electric counterbalance forklift** lifts loads on forks at the front and balances them with the mass of the chassis, counterweight and battery at the rear. It is the general-purpose forklift.

**Powertrain.** An 80 V lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery supplies AC motor controllers. The rear wheels steer through a hydraulic or electric power-steering system. Lifting is handled by its own AC motor driving a hydraulic gear pump.

**Hydraulics and mast.** A multi-spool valve sends pump oil to the lift cylinders, the tilt cylinders and any auxiliary functions, such as a side-shift or fork positioner. Two-stage (duplex) masts suit most loading work. Three-stage (triplex) full-free-lift masts reach higher racking while staying low enough to enter containers.

**Regeneration.** When the truck slows or lowers a load, its traction motors act as generators and feed energy back to the battery. This extends running time and saves brake linings.

**Battery, BMS and charging.** The BMS balances cells, monitors temperature and current, and talks to the matched charger. Because LFP tolerates partial charging, the truck can be topped up during breaks and shift changes rather than having its battery swapped.

**Load centre and stability.** Capacity is rated at a set load centre, usually 500 mm on these models. Moving the load's centre further from the fork face, lifting higher or tilting forward reduces the safe load. The front axle and rear steer-axle pivot form the stability triangle, and the truck and load's centre of gravity must stay within it.

keyComponents.name: AC traction motor(s)
keyComponents.role: Drive the front axle; dual-motor versions give stronger acceleration and gradeability.

keyComponents.name: Hydraulic pump motor
keyComponents.role: Drives the gear pump that powers lifting, tilting and attachments.

keyComponents.name: Mast (duplex or triplex)
keyComponents.role: Raises the fork carriage; full free lift keeps overall height low while lifting.

keyComponents.name: 80 V LFP battery and BMS
keyComponents.role: Stores energy and manages cell balance, temperature and charge state.

keyComponents.name: Motor controllers
keyComponents.role: Convert battery DC into variable AC to control motor speed and torque, including regeneration.

keyComponents.name: Steer axle
keyComponents.role: Rear axle that steers the truck and forms the rear pivot of the stability triangle.

keyComponents.name: Matched charger
keyComponents.role: External BYD charger, sized for the battery and the time available to charge.

applications: Truck loading and pallet movement at FMCG and beverage distribution centres
Brewery and bottling plant warehouses handling crates and shrink-wrapped pallets
Manufacturing plants moving raw materials and finished goods
Covered port warehouses, bonded terminals and container freight stations
Cold-room entry and dock work, subject to BYD confirming the configuration
choosingTips: List your heaviest load and its centre of gravity, then choose capacity at that load centre plus a margin for attachments such as side-shifts, which reduce net capacity.
Pick mast height from the top beam level plus around 150–200 mm of clearance, and check the residual capacity at that height.
Measure aisles: a counterbalance truck needs an aisle wider than its turning radius plus pallet length and safety clearance.
For outdoor use in rain or on rough yards, ask about tyre type, protection rating and sealed components.
Choose battery capacity and charger rating together: a larger pack or faster charger lets a truck cover two shifts with only break-time charging.
Check that your mains or generator supply can carry the charger input. Unstable voltage can trip chargers or damage electronics, so plan surge protection and correct earthing.

dailyChecks: Visual inspection for oil leaks, damaged forks, chains, hoses and tyres
Battery charge level and BMS/fault messages on the display
Charger plug, cable and socket condition
Brakes, parking brake and steering response
Horn, lights, reversing alarm and warning lights
Seatbelt and operator-presence system
Mast lift, tilt and side-shift through full travel

tasks: Inspect forks, heel wear, locking pins and carriage; check fork tips for cracks
Check mast chains for wear, elongation and lubrication; adjust tension evenly
Inspect hydraulic hoses, fittings and cylinders for leaks; check hydraulic oil level
Check tyres and wheel nuts; inspect steering axle and linkages
Test service and parking brakes, horn, lights, alarms and seat/operator-presence switch
Clean dust from motor and controller cooling areas; inspect cable insulation and battery connector
Read the display / diagnostic log for stored fault codes and battery warnings
All 250-hour tasks
Lubricate mast rollers, pivots, steering knuckles and tilt cylinder pins
Check drive axle / gearbox oil level
Inspect mast rollers, side-shift and fork carriage for play
Torque-check main electrical terminals and inspect contactors (where fitted)
All 500-hour tasks
Replace hydraulic return filter / breather as specified
Inspect brake components and wear
Check steering wheel bearings and steer-axle bearings
Verify charger output, cabling and plug condition
All 1,000-hour tasks
Change hydraulic oil and drive-axle / gearbox oil
Measure mast chain elongation against the wear limit; replace if required
Full load test and inspection of overhead guard and structural welds

maintenance.note: Indicative intervals based on general industry practice for electric forklifts, not a BYD-published schedule. Always follow the manufacturer's operation & maintenance manual and adjust for duty cycle, dust, heat and humidity.

safety: Operate within the load chart; capacity reduces with height and longer load centres.
Keep the load uphill when travelling on ramps, and never turn on a slope.
Travel with forks 100–200 mm above the ground and the mast tilted back.
Always wear the seatbelt and keep limbs inside the overhead guard.
Use spotters and marked pedestrian walkways in busy loading bays.
Lower forks fully, set the parking brake and switch off before leaving the truck.

faq.q: How long does a BYD forklift run on one charge?
faq.a: Runtime depends on load, travel distance, lift height and temperature. Most users top up during breaks rather than running the battery down. We estimate runtime for your duty cycle during a site assessment.

faq.q: Can electric forklifts work outdoors?
faq.a: Yes, on paved yards and in light rain when the truck is specified for it. Very rough ground, deep water and heavy loads outdoors may call for a heavy-duty model.

faq.q: Is lithium safer than lead-acid?
faq.a: LFP chemistry is thermally stable and emits no gas while charging, so no dedicated ventilated charging room is needed. As with any battery, safety depends on the approved charger, an intact pack and correct use.

faq.q: How should we look after the lithium battery?
faq.a: LFP batteries need no watering or equalising, but care still matters: charge only with the matched BYD charger for the battery; mismatched chargers bypass the BMS logic; opportunity-charge at breaks rather than running the pack until the truck limits performance; keep the charging plug, connector pins and cables clean, dry and undamaged; if a truck will stand idle for weeks, leave it at a partial state of charge and switch off per the manual; record BMS warnings shown on the display and have them diagnosed promptly.

faq.q: What warranty applies?
faq.a: Warranty terms vary by market and model. Ask us for the terms that apply in Nigeria.

families.name: Heavy-Duty Counterbalance Trucks
families.summary: 6–8 t electric counterbalance trucks for heavy pallets, steel, ports and outdoor yards, replacing large diesel trucks without exhaust fumes.
families.howItWorks:
A **heavy-duty electric counterbalance forklift** does the work of a large diesel truck: steel coils, bagged commodities, beverage pallets in pairs, machinery and container-yard tasks. The layout is the same as a standard counterbalance truck. Forks lift at the front, and the counterweight and battery at the rear keep it balanced. Every major part is scaled up for heavier loads and outdoor duty.

**Power.** These trucks carry large 80 V lithium iron phosphate (LFP) packs. BYD fits 1,080 Ah packs on its 6–8 t trucks, which store far more energy than a light forklift. Two high-power AC traction motors drive the front axle, and a separate AC motor runs the hydraulic pump for lifting, tilting and attachments.

**Brakes and regeneration.** Heavy loads need strong, durable braking. BYD's 6–8 t trucks use oil-immersed disc brakes, which run sealed in oil and resist dust and water. Regenerative braking on the traction motors puts energy back into the battery whenever the truck slows.

**Mast and tyres.** Masts are heavier-section duplex or triplex designs, and they often carry attachments such as side-shifts, fork positioners or clamps. These trucks usually run on large pneumatic or solid tyres for yards, and BYD notes that its tallest masts on the 6–8 t trucks need widened tyres.

**Charging.** Large packs need high-current chargers. BYD fits 200 A as standard on the 6–8 t trucks, with 400 A fast charging as an option. Planning the charger supply is therefore part of choosing the truck.

**Stability.** Capacity is rated at the load centre shown on the data plate (600 mm for BYD's 6–8 t trucks). Long or bulky loads, attachments and high lifts all reduce the safe capacity.

keyComponents.role: Large pack of up to 1,080 Ah on the 6–8 t trucks, giving long running time on heavy work.

keyComponents.name: Dual AC traction motors
keyComponents.role: Provide the torque needed for heavy loads, ramps and outdoor yards.

keyComponents.name: Oil-immersed disc brakes
keyComponents.role: Sealed wet brakes on the 6–8 t trucks that resist dust and water and have a long service life.

keyComponents.role: Carries heavy loads and attachments such as clamps or fork positioners.

keyComponents.name: High-current charger
keyComponents.role: 200 A or 400 A charger sized to recharge a large pack within a break or shift change.

keyComponents.name: Optional operator cab
keyComponents.role: Enclosed cab for weather protection on outdoor duty.

Deduct attachment weight and its effect on load centre from the truck's rated capacity.

Size the battery and charger to the shift pattern. A 400 A charger cuts charging time but needs a strong supply, so plan the supply before you order.
Check the site power supply: high-current chargers need a suitable three-phase supply or a generator sized and protected for it.
Consider service access. These trucks are often far from a workshop, which suits on-site maintenance.

faq.q: Can an electric forklift really replace a 6–8 t diesel?
faq.a: For many duties, yes. BYD builds 6–8 t trucks with large LFP packs and fast-charge options. We compare your current diesel duty cycle before recommending a model.

faq.q: What power supply do I need for a 400 A charger?
faq.a: High-current chargers draw significant power and typically need a three-phase supply. We assess your mains or generator capacity, protection and cabling before installation.

faq.q: Can it work in the rain?

families.name: Reach Trucks
families.summary: Narrow-aisle electric trucks that reach into racking and lift high, packing more storage into the same warehouse floor.
families.howItWorks:
A **reach truck** is designed to store pallets high in narrow aisles. A counterbalance forklift carries its load in front of the front wheels and needs a wide aisle to turn. A reach truck instead has two **outrigger legs** with load wheels that stretch forward from the chassis. The mast moves forward along the legs (a **moving-mast** design) to pick or place a pallet, then pulls back so the load sits within the truck's wheelbase while it travels and turns.

**Why it needs less space.** The load is carried inside the footprint and the truck pivots around a central drive wheel, so it can make a right-angle turn into racking in a much narrower aisle than a counterbalance truck. Lift heights are usually higher too, using three-stage masts.

**Drive and hydraulics.** A single steered drive wheel under the operator compartment is powered by an AC traction motor. A separate pump motor supplies the hydraulic circuit for lift, reach, tilt and side-shift. The operator sits sideways or stands, depending on the model, so both travel directions are easy to see.

**Battery.** BYD's reach trucks use lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries. The RTR series uses 80 V packs and the R15PS/R18PS models use 48 V packs. Because LFP accepts opportunity charging, operators can top up at breaks instead of changing batteries. The BMS manages cell balance and temperature.

**Height and stability.** At height, the truck's capacity falls and the mast flexes more. Reach trucks therefore have load charts specific to each mast and height. Many also use speed and lift-height interlocks, and some offer height pre-selection or tilt-at-height limits.

faq.q: How much narrower are reach-truck aisles?
faq.a: It depends on pallet size and truck model. Reach trucks typically work in clearly narrower aisles than counterbalance forklifts. We calculate the required aisle from the model data and your pallets.

faq.q: Can a reach truck load lorries?
faq.a: Not normally. Reach trucks are designed for smooth indoor floors and racking. Use a counterbalance forklift for trailers and outdoor docks.

faq.q: How should we look after the lithium battery?
faq.a: LFP batteries need no watering or equalising, but care still matters: charge only with the matched BYD charger for the battery; mismatched chargers bypass the BMS logic; opportunity-charge at breaks rather than running the pack until the truck limits performance; keep the charging plug, connector pins and cables clean, dry and undamaged; if a truck will stand idle for weeks, leave it at a partial state of charge and switch off per the manual; record BMS warnings shown on the display and have them diagnosed promptly.

faq.q: What warranty applies?
faq.a: Warranty terms vary by market and model. Ask us for the terms that apply in Nigeria.

families.name: Pallet Stackers
families.summary: Compact 1.4 t electric stackers that lift pallets onto racking where a full forklift is too big or not justified.
families.howItWorks:
An **electric pallet stacker** sits between a pallet truck and a forklift. Like a pallet truck, it uses a tiller and a single steered drive wheel. It also has a **mast**, so it can lift pallets onto racking, mezzanines and truck beds.

**Stability without a counterweight.** Most stackers do not balance the load with a heavy counterweight. They use **straddle legs** or base arms with load wheels under or around the pallet. The load sits inside the truck's wheelbase, which keeps the stacker short and light. Because of this, the pallet type and rack bottom beam must suit the leg design.

**Lift system.** An AC or DC pump motor drives a hydraulic pump. The pump feeds the lift cylinder or cylinders, which extend a two- or three-stage mast through chains and pulleys. A proportional valve controls the lowering speed. Some models have an **initial lift**: the base arms rise a little on their own, so the truck can carry two pallets at once (one on the arms, one on the forks) or clear uneven dock plates.

**Drive and braking.** An AC traction motor drives the steered wheel, and the controller provides regenerative slowing. An electromagnetic brake applies when the tiller is released or moved to its upper or lower position.

**Battery and charging.** BYD's stackers run on 24 V lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries with a BMS. Ask us which charger suits your shifts. Short charges during breaks keep the truck working through a shift.

**Operator position.** Pedestrian stackers suit occasional lifting. Stand-on models with fold-down platforms and side guards cover longer distances at higher speed.

faq.q: Stacker or forklift?
faq.a: A stacker is lighter, more compact and lower-cost to run for moderate lifting volumes and indoor floors. A counterbalance forklift is better for loading trucks from ground level, outdoor use and heavier or more frequent lifting.

faq.q: Can a stacker carry two pallets?
faq.a: Ask us which stacker suits your pallets and racking.

faq.q: How should we look after the lithium battery?
faq.a: LFP batteries need no watering or equalising, but care still matters: charge only with the matched BYD charger for the battery; mismatched chargers bypass the BMS logic; opportunity-charge at breaks rather than running the pack until the truck limits performance; keep the charging plug, connector pins and cables clean, dry and undamaged; if a truck will stand idle for weeks, leave it at a partial state of charge and switch off per the manual; record BMS warnings shown on the display and have them diagnosed promptly.

families.name: Pallet Trucks
families.summary: Powered 2 t pallet trucks, walk-behind or stand-on, for moving pallets quickly across warehouse floors and loading docks.
families.howItWorks:
An **electric pallet truck** (powered pallet jack) moves pallets across the floor. It lifts a pallet only a short way, just enough to clear the ground, and is not built for stacking. The operator walks behind it or stands on a platform and steers with a **tiller arm** that holds all the controls: travel direction and speed, lift and lower, horn, and a belly-button reversing switch for safety.

**Drive.** A single drive wheel under the power unit is driven by an AC traction motor and steered by the tiller. Two load wheels under the fork tips carry the pallet. Releasing the tiller or pushing it to the upper or lower position applies an electromagnetic brake. Lifting off the throttle gives regenerative slowing.

**Lift.** A small electric hydraulic power pack pushes a cylinder that raises the fork frame. Linkage rods running along each fork push the load wheels down at the same time, so the whole pallet lifts evenly.

**Battery.** BYD pallet trucks run on 24 V lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries. Many have an on-board charger that plugs into a normal socket, so the truck can be charged anywhere during a break. The battery management system (BMS) protects the cells from over-charge, over-discharge and overheating.

**Variants.** Walkie (pedestrian) trucks suit short runs and tight spaces. Stand-on platform trucks are faster and suit longer distances, such as dock-to-store runs in large distribution centres. BYD also offers pallet trucks with higher lift for working at waist height in retail stores.

families.name: Towing Tractors
families.summary: Battery-electric tugs from 3 t to 25 t towing capacity for moving trains of trailers in factories, ports and logistics hubs.
families.howItWorks:
An **electric tow tractor** (tug) pulls loads on trailers or carts instead of lifting them. One tractor can move a train of several trailers, so it can replace many forklift trips over long internal routes: between production halls, from warehouse to dispatch, or across port and airport aprons.

**Drawbar pull, not lift.** A tractor is rated by the **towed load** it can pull on level ground. It works by putting traction through its drive wheels, which needs weight on those wheels. Tractors are therefore heavy for their size, and the towing rating drops on slopes and slippery surfaces. A tow coupling at the rear connects the trailers, and a pin or automatic hitch is common.

**Drive.** An AC traction motor drives the wheels through a reduction gearbox and differential, with the speed controlled electronically. When the operator eases off, regenerative braking slows the tractor and train and puts energy back into the battery. Mechanical service and parking brakes hold the train. The larger tractors have hill-hold and slope protection.

**Sizes.** Compact pedestrian or stand-on tugs (around 3–5 t towed) move carts in assembly plants and hospitals. Seated and cab tractors (25 t) haul heavy trailer trains outdoors.

**Battery.** BYD's tractors use lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries: 24–48 V on the small tugs and 80 V on the large tractors. Long routes make tractors good candidates for opportunity charging at the end of each loop. The BMS keeps the pack within safe limits.

Allow for gradients and floor surface: towing capacity on a ramp is far below the level-ground rating.
Check that trailers have suitable brakes, couplings and castors for the speed and load.

faq.q: Why use a tractor instead of a forklift?
faq.a: For long, repeated routes, one tractor pulling several trailers moves more material per trip than a forklift carrying one pallet, with less wear and energy use.

faq.q: Does the towing rating apply on a ramp?
faq.a: No. Ratings are normally for level ground. Gradients reduce the load a tractor can safely pull and stop. We check your routes during assessment.
